subject: Intermittent streaming stalls — suspected header reassembly bug in client SDK
messages:
From: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@greenleafhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: streaming — intermittent stalls since SDK update

Hi Laura,

Since we upgraded to the client SDK 2.4.1 two days ago, our production integration with Redwood is showing intermittent stalls during streamed responses and a spike in 502/stream-reset errors. The behaviour is inconsistent — some requests stream successfully, others hang for 10–30s and then fail with a client-side "stream-stalled" error.

We captured some client-side traces and a short server-side trace (attached). The client trace shows repeated "incomplete-header" events right before the stall. Our integration team suspects the parser may be dropping header fragments when packets align a certain way. This started immediately after the SDK update.

Can we get help on this urgently — this is impacting live patient-facing flows.

Attachments: client-trace-20261201.txt

Thanks,
Tom Barnes
Director of Engineering
Greenleaf Health

Subject: Re: streaming — intermittent stalls since SDK update

Quick triage summary (internal):

What I see in the edge logs: repeated InvalidHeaderException entries correlated with a subset of the failing requests. The exception is thrown inside the streaming parser when it attempts to parse headers but the buffer only contains a partial header frame. The edge receives the stream frames correctly, but our parser currently assumes headers arrive atomically for the first chunk and doesn't reassemble across read boundaries in one code path.

Repro steps I used:
1) Run local harness against SDK 2.4.1 with network throttling (small MTU and inter-packet delay).
2) Force boundary such that Content-Type header is split across TCP reads.
3) Observe parser hitting InvalidHeaderException and client observability shows "stream-stalled" when server attempts to write more frames.

Temporary mitigation possibilities:
- Server-side: relax strict header parsing and accept partial header reassembly for Greenleaf's IPs.
- Client-side: patch SDK to reassemble header fragments before parse (will be 2.4.3).

I'll attach the heap dump and a trimmed rx trace that reproduces locally. Will aim for a hotfix branch today and a patched SDK tomorrow.

Attachments: heapdump_20261202.log, sdk-rxtrace-frames.zip

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: exec attention requested — Greenleaf production outages

Update and proposed remediation (final):

Root cause: an off-by-one handling in the streaming parser's header reassembly code path that only manifests when a header token is split across network read boundaries (exacerbated by the small-packet patterns in Greenleaf's client environment and the 2.4.1 SDK framing change). The parser dropped the partial fragment rather than buffering it, causing InvalidHeaderException and the stream to stall.

Work done:
- Engineering: created hotfix branch and backported a parser reassembly fix to the serving edge (hotfix id: sup-9821-hotfix). Deployed to a canary pool that routes only Greenleaf traffic.
- SDK: implemented robust reassembly and added unit/integration tests; SDK 2.4.3 will be released tomorrow with patch notes.
- Mitigation: server-side fallback now accepts partial header sequence and will attempt reassembly for in-flight streams from whitelisted subnets.

Customer impact & timeline:
- Canary deployed 2026-12-05 15:30 PT — immediate reduction in 502s and stalled streams observed.
- Full rollout pending QA (estimated 24–36 hours).
- Recommend Greenleaf apply SDK 2.4.3 in staging as soon as it's available; we'll coordinate a joint production cutover.

Attachments: redwood_debug_trace_20261202.json

Next steps: Connor/Marissa to confirm the production cutover window with Greenleaf and whether they want an SLA credit proposal. Laura: happy to draft the exec update for the Greenleaf CTO.

—Rishi
